companions.name: M31V J00443610+4129194 B
companions.description: The secondary star of M31V J00443610+4129194, an eclipsing pair of hot stars in the Andromeda Galaxy, 15.4 solar masses and 5.6 solar radii; the two eclipse each other every 2.048644 days.

radius.source: Secondary radius 5.6 +/- 0.4 solar radii, Vilardell et al. (2010), A&A 509, A70, Table 2

mass.source: Secondary mass 15.4 +/- 1.2 solar masses, Vilardell et al. (2010), A&A 509, A70, Table 2

temperature.source: Secondary Teff 30100 +/- 900 K, Vilardell et al. (2010), A&A 509, A70, Table 3

orbit.source: M31V J00443610+4129194: P 2.048644 d, time of primary minimum HJD 2452908.694, i 69.9 degrees and a 22.6 +/- 0.5 solar radii (Vilardell et al. (2010), A&A 509, A70, Table 2); the fit follows the procedure of Ribas et al. (2005), which adopts a circular orbit, in a semi-detached configuration (Sect. 4). a/R = 22.6/9.2 = 2.4565 primary radii. HJD is taken as BJD_TDB (under a minute apart); at the primary minimum the primary is eclipsed, so the secondary is in front.

text.card: The secondary star of an eclipsing pair in the Andromeda Galaxy, one orbit every 2.048644 days.
text.introduction: It has 15.4 solar masses and 5.6 solar radii; its partner has 21.7 and 9.2. The pair gave a direct distance to the galaxy: 724 kiloparsecs.
text.locator: Vilardell et al. (2010), A&A 509, A70, Table 2: M, R, P and the distance
